output.answer: No — Discord is not publicly traded as of November 11, 2026. It remains a private, venture-backed company, but it is actively moving toward an IPO: Bloomberg reported on January 6, 2026 that Discord had confidentially filed for a U.S. IPO with Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan as underwriters, and TechCrunch reported the company targeted a March 2026 debut. However, that target slipped — as of October 30, 2026, ten months after the filing, Discord is still private and its registration statement has not been made public, so its shares cannot yet be bought on any stock exchange.
caveats: The confidential IPO filing and the March 2026 debut target were reported by Bloomberg and TechCrunch citing people familiar with the matter, not confirmed by Discord itself; IPO plans can be revised, delayed, or abandoned, and no new listing date has been reported since the March target slipped.

Because the registration statement is still confidential, there is no verified public valuation, exchange, price range, or share count; recent valuation marks ($23.51–$36.79 per share, implying roughly $6.4–$10 billion) come from investor fund reports and secondary-market trackers, not from Discord.

An IPO could still complete soon: under SEC rules the registration statement must go public at least 15 days before roadshow marketing, so Discord cannot be traded publicly until at least that point, but once it does the answer changes.

passages.quote: Ten months after the filing, the chat app is still private, and its paperwork still hasn't been made public.
Discord Inc. filed confidentially for an initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter, adding to a rapidly growing pipeline of venture capital-backed tech listings.

Discord, the popular chat and community platform, filed confidential IPO paperwork with the SEC and has pinned its hopes on a debut in March, sources told Bloomberg. The company hired top-tier tech IPO bankers Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase as its underwriters.

A listing can't happen quickly from here. Under SEC rules, a company that files in private has to make its registration statement public at least 15 days before it starts pitching the shares to investors. Discord hadn't done that by 30 October, so an IPO is weeks away at the earliest, and no new date has been reported.

output.question: Is Discord publicly traded?

key_facts.fact: As of October 30, 2026, Discord is still a private company — ten months after its confidential IPO filing, its registration statement has not been made public and no listing has occurred.
Discord filed confidentially for a U.S. initial public offering, working with Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase as underwriters; the company has more than 200 million monthly users.
Discord reportedly targeted a March 2026 IPO debut, which later slipped; Discord was last valued at $14.7 billion in its 2021 funding round, in which it raised $500 million.
Discord had been working with Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan on a planned IPO as early as March 2025, but no filing or scheduled offering existed at that time.

Since the IPO stalled, investors mark Discord at widely divergent prices: Fidelity funds value its Series I preferred shares at $23.51 each (as of August 31, 2026), and secondary-market tracker Forge put the indicative price at $36.79 on October 30, 2026, implying a value of about $10.02 billion — all below the ~$55.06 per share (~$15 billion valuation) of the 2021 round.
